statement: An employer and employee can agree to a trial period only when it lasts no longer than 90 calendar days, the employee has not worked for the employer before, and the trial period is at the start of the employment; the trial period is not valid if the employee does not sign the employment agreement before starting work, and in most cases an employee dismissed during a valid trial period cannot raise a personal grievance for unjustified dismissal.
caveat: The current Employment New Zealand guidance carries no employer-size limit on trial periods (the earlier small-employer cap no longer appears); procedural defects such as the employee starting work before signing revive the personal-grievance route. The provisions are Employment Relations Act 2000 ss 67A-67B (legislation.govt.nz answers automated fetches with an AWS WAF challenge, recorded 2026-10-23). Check the live guidance before relying.
